title: Feature fleet costing & headcount stitchbook
content:
Executive summary:

This stitchbook ties together feature-level GPU and infra cost forecasts, role-level headcount plans, and a three-scenario pricing-sensitivity matrix to produce a short-to-medium runway impact view. Purpose is to give product, eng and finance a single working sheet for (1) deciding which feature fleets to prioritize for quantization/batching work, (2) estimating hiring vs contract tradeoffs, and (3) understanding token-price elasticity on margin and runway.

Primary assumptions (base case):
- Time horizon: next 12 months (Dec 2026 — Nov 2027)
- Currency: USD
- Average FTE fully-loaded cost by role (annual): Staff SWE $220k, ML SWE $240k, Infra Eng $200k, SRE $195k, Product PM $180k, Data Scientist $190k
- GPU cost (effective blended run-rate): $0.62 / vGPU-hour (post-commit mix across regions), monthly amortized reserved + spot mix
- Token intensity per feature: estimated tokens per 1k calls (see table)
- Serving efficiency improvements: quantization reduces per-token GPU time by 28% (when applied)

Feature fleet table (monthlyized view) — sample rows, multiply by 12 for annual: 

Feature | Monthly calls (k) | Tokens per call | Tokens/month (M) | GPU-hours/month (est) | Notes
Search-rerank | 1,200 | 120 | 144.0 | 9.6k GPU-hrs (baseline batching)
Customer-chat | 400 | 680 | 272.0 | 18.1k GPU-hrs (kv-cache heavy)
Doc-embed-index | 150 | 2,000 | 300.0 | 10.8k GPU-hrs (embedding optimized)
Saas-assist-auto | 60 | 9,500 | 570.0 | 38.0k GPU-hrs (long-context tails)

Notes on derivation: GPU-hours estimate uses observed token/sec per instance matrix from serving-runtime and adds 8% infra overhead and 5% overhead for retries. Long-context workloads have much lower effective tokens/sec so cost skews high.

Headcount stitch (recommended hires / contractors by quarter):
- Q1 hires: 2 ML SWE (mid), 1 Infra Eng (senior contractor), 1 PM (assoc)
- Q2 hires: 1 SRE (mid), 1 Data Scientist (contract-to-hire)
- Q3 hires: 1 Staff SWE (senior) for embedding optimization, swap 1 contractor infra -> perm as usage stabilizes
- Q4: freeze for runway watch unless ARR conversion meets targets

Quarterly headcount cost snapshot (monthly equivalent in USD):
Role | Headcount (FTE) | Monthly fully-loaded cost per FTE | Monthly subtotal
ML SWE | 3 | 20,000 | 60,000
Staff SWE | 2 | 18,333 | 36,666
Infra Eng | 2 | 16,667 | 33,334
SRE | 1 | 16,250 | 16,250
Product PM | 1 | 15,000 | 15,000
Data Scientist | 1 | 15,833 | 15,833
Contractors (infra + data) | 1.8 | 12,000 avg | 21,600
TOTAL MONTHLY PAYROLL 
(rounded) |  |  | 198,683

Project-level cost allocation: payroll (above) + GPU cost (monthly) + infra egress/storage overhead (monthly) + monitoring/logging spend (monthly) + misc lic/third-party. Base monthly overhead estimate: GPU cost (combined features in table) = 77,300 USD; infra & logs 8,500 USD; misc third-party 3,200 USD. Combined monthly feature fleet cost (base) = 198,683 + 77,300 + 8,500 + 3,200 = 287,683 USD.

Three-scenario pricing sensitivity (impact on monthly margin and runway):
Assumptions: current revenue linked to token usage for these fleets is $0.0009 per token (base). Scenarios adjust price per token and headcount ramping:
- Conservative: token price falls 20% vs base (-20%), hiring slowed (only 40% of planned hires)
- Base: token price unchanged, hires per plan
- Aggressive: token price +15% vs base, faster conversion to paid customers (+8% revenue uplift), full hires

Sensitivity table (monthly):
Scenario | Token price | Revenue (est) | Monthly cost | Net margin | Runway delta (vs base)
Conservative | $0.00072 | $673,200 | $256,400 | $416,800 (note: this line is net of feature costs only) | -1.8 weeks
Base | $0.00090 | $840,000 | $287,700 | $552,300 | 0
Aggressive | $0.001035 | $987,600 | $310,500 | $677,100 | +3.1 weeks

Interpretation and recommended actions (short bullets):
- Immediate: prioritize quantization for Saas-assist-auto and Customer-chat — these two account for ~70% of GPU-hours and show the largest per-token savings potential. A focused 90-day project could reduce fleet GPU-hours by ~22% and improve runway by ~2–3 weeks in base case.
- Hiring vs contracting: delay permanent senior Staff SWE hire until Q3 but onboard contractors for infra optimization in Q1 to accelerate kernel & batching improvements with lower near-term cash burn.
- Pricing levers: introduce usage-tiered pricing for long-context features (Saas-assist-auto) where marginal cost is highest. A small floor (e.g., +10–20% for >1k token calls) preserves margin while retaining volume for low-intensity features.
- Feature gating: implement a soft throttle for tail long-context generation when GPU utilization > 85% to avoid burst-driven margin erosion.

Open questions / items to validate:
- Re-run token/sec microbenchmarks after next runtime release (v1.13) — current numbers may shift with new kernel schedule.
- Confirm GPU blended rate with infra ops for planned region mix (US-EAST heavy vs EU fallback).
- Validate customer elasticity with a small price experiment for long-context tier in Q2 (A/B test 5% vs 15% uplift).

Appendix: quick sensitivity math (how runway delta computed)
- Runway delta is derived from net margin changes normalized to monthly cash cushion bucket (current cash allocation to feature fleet = 2.5M). Runway weeks delta = (delta_monthly_margin * 12 months) / (monthly burn) * 52 weeks proportion, simplified to an approximate weeks figure for planning.

Notes to reviewers: this is a working sheet. Numbers are intentionally rounded for readibility. Please add rows for any additional features you want included (esp. partner integrations) and flag any contractual GPU commitments not reflected here.

Version history: created 2026-11-04 by Asha Patel. Edits: 2026-11-12 (added contractor plan), 2026-11-18 (updated GPU blended rate and scenario numbers).
